title: Additivity of invariant infinitesimal coefficients
statement: For an arbitrary scheme $S$ and group scheme $G/S$ [def-sc-group-scheme], let $v,w$ be points over the dual-number thickening $S[\epsilon]$ [def-sc-dual-numbers] reducing to the identity. For every open $U$ of $G$, define $D_v(U)$ by the $\epsilon$ coefficient of the comorphism of $(g,\epsilon)\mapsto g v(\epsilon)$; the inverse image of $U$ is $U$, so this is an additive endomorphism of $\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_G)$. Then $D_{vw}=D_v+D_w$ on every open. No affine, field, smoothness or characteristic hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Lie-ring obligation docstrings, invariant-extension and mixed-coefficient steps (blueprint sk-d-tangent).

proof.text: Construct the right translation of the universal point explicitly from the projection G[epsilon] to G and the pullback of v along G to S. Its zero section is the identity, so its comorphism is a + epsilon D_v(a) on each open.

Associativity identifies translation by v*w with the successive translations by v and w over the same parameter. Their lifts fix epsilon. Composing a + epsilon D_v(a) and a + epsilon D_w(a) adds the two coefficients, since the cross term has epsilon squared. Take the coefficients on every open.
